explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/806: for A ⊆ {1,…,n} with |A| ≤ n^{1/2}, must there be B ⊂ ℤ with |B| = o(n^{1/2}) and A ⊆ B + B? The answer is yes (Alon–Bukh–Sudakov). The statement says: for every ε > 0, eventually in n, every such A has some B ⊆ ℤ with A ⊆ B + B and |B| ≤ ε√n. That is the uniform-in-A reading of o(n^{1/2}), which is the intended one and is what ABS prove. Faithful.
